title: objectql read path: a declared column the driver did not return stays an absent key, so mongo/memory rows are sparse where SQL rows are not
body:
domain:devx#2 · marchtian · session_017ihL2gLghEqeDKTbDTC7Zd

Filing gate: ① a measured cross-driver gap, named as follow-up D.1 of the #29094 ruling (option A, maintainer 「同意」, ruling comment 6579342813). Non-blocking, so it is filed as p3.
Reader: `domain:server`, `packages/objectql/src/declared-read-columns.ts` and the engine's read path that calls it.
Dedupe (open AND closed): "materializeDeclaredFields null driver" → #8489, #9276 and #4953 (all closed; #9276 is the `undefined`-valued own key, a different shape). "declared column absent mongo read null" → none. None fills an absent declared column on read.
reach: any object served by the mongo or memory driver whose row was inserted without a value for a declared field, read through REST or the engine.
type: Bug

Business reason: the same record reads differently by driver. SQL answers a declared column as `null`, while mongo and memory leave the key out. A client predicate such as an action `visible` faults on the missing key and hides the button. #29094 keeps that surface sparse by ruling, but a column the read named, and whose persisted state is in hand, has no reason to be absent.

## What the code does on `main`
- `withDeclaredColumnsOnly` / `rowsWithDeclaredColumnsOnly` (`packages/objectql/src/declared-read-columns.ts`, around line 106) only remove keys outside the declared set. They never add a declared key the driver left out.
- `packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/src/mongodb-driver.ts` (around lines 83–85) says nothing is stored for a field given no value, so the row has no key for a field that was never written. The memory driver keeps stored null and absent key apart in the same way.

## Wanted
When the read selects a declared column (an explicit `$select` that names it, or a whole-record GET), and the driver returns no key for it, the engine answers `null`. That matches the "IN HAND" rule of `materializeDeclaredFields`: the persisted state is in hand, so `null` is honest. Columns the read did not select stay absent, and so do columns that field-level security refused. Pin the result across SQL, mongo and memory.
